_note: Teardown/breakdown data for the Showroom's exploded view. This GLB is PALETTE-MERGED — 6 generic PaletteMaterial00N groups with no isolated wheels/interior/lights/engine. Degraded teardown: the painted shell (PaletteMaterial002, the full body; also the paint target) plus the surrounding panels/glass/trim lift as `body`, the lower mass (PaletteMaterial003) drops as `chassis`, a procedural suspension stand-in spreads, and the RWD internals + interior + lights are honest info-callouts (ids NOT engine/drivetrain so no wrong FWD geometry renders). Anchors in FITTED car space (~3.4 units long, +X nose, +Y up, +Z left). Copy grounded on data/cars/19-bmw-m3-e46.json; anchors from frontend/scripts/model_meshes.mjs.

parts.label: Body, Aero & Glass
parts.summary: The steel unibody coupe with the M3's flared arches — now an appreciating modern classic.
parts.detail: Steel unibody coupe (or convertible) with the M3's subtly flared arches and power dome — a shape that has aged into an appreciating modern classic.
parts.watch: The signature E46 M3 flaw: rear subframe mounting points crack where they meet the chassis floor — inspect and reinforce with plates.

parts.label: Chassis & Underbody
parts.summary: The floorpan and lower structure — home of the E46 M3's infamous subframe mounts.
parts.detail: The lower body structure and floorpan that carry the rear subframe mounts — the defining E46 M3 weak point, where the chassis cracks under hard use.
parts.watch: Have the rear subframe mounting points inspected for cracks and reinforced with plates — this is the make-or-break check on any E46 M3.

parts.label: 3.2L S54 Inline-Six
parts.summary: One of the all-time-great naturally aspirated sixes — 333 hp screaming to 8,000 rpm.
parts.detail: S54B32 — 3.2L naturally aspirated inline-six with six individual throttle bodies and double-VANOS, 333 hp (US) at a screaming 8,000 rpm. (Info callout — this merged model has no separate engine mesh.)
parts.watch: Rod bearings wear from tight factory clearances — preventive replacement is the accepted fix — plus VANOS rattle and aging cooling-system plastics.

parts.label: Getrag 6-Speed & LSD (RWD)
parts.summary: A Getrag six-speed (or the clunky SMG) driving the rear wheels through a limited-slip diff.
parts.detail: Getrag 420G 6-speed manual or the automated-clutch SMG II, driving the rear wheels through a limited-slip differential. (Info callout — not a separate mesh in this model.)
parts.watch: SMG hydraulic pump and actuator failures plague SMG cars; many owners convert to the manual.

parts.label: Strut Front / Multilink Rear
parts.summary: MacPherson-strut front and multilink rear — the benchmark sport-coupe chassis.
parts.detail: MacPherson-strut front and multilink rear — the sharp, communicative chassis that set the sport-coupe benchmark. (Shown as a procedural stand-in — not a separate mesh in this model.)
parts.watch: Worn front control-arm and rear trailing-arm bushings dull the steering; refresh them with age.

parts.label: 18" Wheels & Tires
parts.summary: Staggered 18" alloys on wide rubber — the footprint that puts 333 hp down.
parts.detail: Factory staggered 18-inch alloys (the double-spoke style-67s) on wide performance tires. (Info callout — the wheels aren't a separable mesh in this model.)
parts.watch: Curb rash on the low-profile rubber; many cars wear the fragile factory finish.

parts.label: Four-Wheel Vented Discs
parts.summary: Vented discs at all four corners — strong and genuinely track-capable.
parts.detail: Vented discs at all four corners — strong and track-capable with the right pads and fluid. (Info callout — not a separable mesh in this model.)
parts.watch: Warped or cracked rotors on track-used cars; upgrade pads and fluid before lapping.

parts.label: Interior & Driver's Cockpit
parts.summary: The driver-focused E46 cockpit — supportive seats and the classic M three-spoke wheel.
parts.detail: The E46 M3's driver-oriented cabin with supportive sport seats, the three-spoke M steering wheel, and the era's clear analog gauges. (Info callout — not a separable mesh in this model.)
parts.watch: Pixel loss in the cluster/on-board-computer display and worn seat bolsters on high-mile cars.

parts.label: Lighting & Electronics
parts.summary: Early-2000s BMW electronics — robust in design, now aging hardware.
parts.detail: Angel-eye halo headlights and the era's BMW electronics — robust in design but now aging. (Info callout — not a separable mesh in this model.)
parts.watch: Failing window regulators, pixel loss in the cluster display, and tired cooling-fan electronics.
